sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: Candidate faithfully preserves the ship target, owner-correct component path, exclusive selector branches, required Boolean evidence and cardinalities, standard and alternative chest obligations, alternative exemption from volume and height checks, declared operands and units, direct calculations, comparison directions, and expected-result-scaled tolerance.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: Remove gen:LinkedInletChestShape: the authoritative target is ship, so inlet-chest constraints must be reached through the ship’s nltl:hasComponent path rather than applied unconditionally to every inletChest in the graph. Split the branch-specific chest shapes. When coolingWaterChestVolumeAndHeightRequirementsCannotBeMet is false, require at least one linked inletChest satisfying the standard location, volume calculation, ice-accumulation height, discharge-pipe, and strainer-area checks. When it is true, require coolingWaterChestAlternativeArrangementUsed=true and at least two linked inletChest nodes with alternatingCoolingWaterIntakeAndDischarge=true, while retaining the non-exempt arrangement/location, discharge, and strainer checks; do not reuse the full standard shape in this branch because that incorrectly makes the exempt paragraph 2 volume and paragraph 3 height requirements mandatory. Keep the formula tolerance based on the expected result and preserve the declared ship-owned operands and selector evidence.

Prevent contradictory Boolean values from creating accidental-pass branch logic. Add sh:maxCount 1 to coolingWaterChestVolumeAndHeightRequirementsCannotBeMet on the ship-level selector constraint and in both sh:or branches, so a ship cannot carry both true and false and select the easier branch. Also add sh:maxCount 1 to coolingWaterChestAlternativeArrangementUsed and to each inlet-chest Boolean constrained with sh:hasValue true (alternatingCoolingWaterIntakeAndDischarge, iceAccumulationSpaceAboveInlet, nearCentrelineAndWellAftIfPossible, and fullCapacityDischargePipeConnected), ensuring that required true evidence cannot coexist with a contradictory false value. Preserve the current ship target, linked-component branch shapes, alternative exemption from the paragraph 2 volume and paragraph 3 height checks, and expected-result-scaled formula tolerances.

Eliminate the accidental-pass split between gen:StandardInletChestShape and gen:StandardChestBranchShape’s existential SPARQL query. Currently one linked chest can satisfy the qualified Core shape while a different chest, potentially with multivalued quantities from which a passing combination is selected, satisfies the formula query. Move the standard recommended-volume and strainer-ratio calculations into a violation-style SPARQL constraint on gen:StandardInletChestShape, obtaining the ship-owned totalRelevantEnginePower through the inverse relationship pattern `?ship nltl:hasComponent $this`, and remove the separate ship-level existential formula query. Then the chest counted by sh:qualifiedMinCount 1 must itself satisfy the location, paragraph 2/3 requirements, discharge connection, cardinalities, units, and both calculations. Preserve the existing expected-result-scaled tolerances, ship target and selector cardinalities, alternative branch with at least two linked chests, and its exemption from the paragraph 2 volume and paragraph 3 height requirements.

Candidate faithfully preserves the ship target, owner-correct component path, exclusive selector branches, required Boolean evidence and cardinalities, standard and alternative chest obligations, alternative exemption from volume and height checks, declared operands and units, direct calculations, comparison directions, and expected-result-scaled tolerance.
